faqs.q: How much does a Caucasian Shepherd Dog cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $1,200–$4,000 for a Caucasian Shepherd Dog puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Caucasian Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Budget $200–$400 per month for a Caucasian Shepherd Dog, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Large breeds cost more across every category — food portions, medication doses and professional services all scale with weight.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Caucasian Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($800–1,200), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($800–1,800 per year). Grooming adds $400–$1,200 annually for Caucasian Shepherd Dogs due to their coat type.

faqs.q: How much does a Caucasian Shepherd Dog cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Caucasian Shepherd Dog are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,500–$5,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Caucasian Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs need brushing 3–5 times per week, daily during seasonal coat blows. The dense undercoat requires a dedicated undercoat rake, not just a surface slicker brush. Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Caucasian Shepherd Dogs shed a lot?
faqs.a: Yes — they are considered heavy shedders. Regular brushing is the most effective control tool. A slicker brush and undercoat rake are both essential for Caucasian Shepherd Dogs. Deshedding treatments from professional groomers can reduce seasonal shedding temporarily.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Caucasian Shepherd Dog need?
faqs.a: A slicker brush for surface debris and an undercoat rake for the dense undercoat are both essential. A shedding blade or deshedding tool helps during heavy moult periods. A nail grinder is useful if your Caucasian Shepherd Dog is sensitive to clippers.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Caucasian Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Caucasian Shepherd Dogs that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Caucasian Shepherd Dogs easy to train?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs are independent thinkers and can be challenging to train. They respond best to high-value rewards and clear, consistent criteria. A structured puppy class from week one is strongly recommended.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Caucasian Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Caucasian Shepherd Dogs. Clicker training with precise timing works well to mark the exact moment of correct behaviour. Avoid aversive methods — they increase anxiety and often create secondary behavioural problems.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Caucasian Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Caucasian Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs can take longer to reach reliable obedience than easier-to-train breeds — expect 3–6 months of consistent daily training for solid basics. Their independent nature means results compound slowly but durably with patience.

faqs.q: What health problems do Caucasian Shepherd Dogs commonly have?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs are most commonly associated with routine age-related conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Caucasian Shepherd Dogs live?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs have an average lifespan of 10–12 years. Larger breeds typically have shorter lifespans than smaller breeds. Maintaining a healthy weight and regular vet care are the most impactful factors for longevity.

faqs.q: Are Caucasian Shepherd Dogs prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Caucasian Shepherd Dog puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Caucasian Shepherd Dog puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Caucasian Shepherd Dog-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Caucasian Shepherd Dogs good with kids?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs can do well with children when properly socialised from puppyhood. Every dog is an individual — early exposure to children's behaviour (noise, sudden movements) is the most effective preparation.

faqs.q: Do Caucasian Shepherd Dogs get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Caucasian Shepherd Dogs bark a lot?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs are not considered excessive barkers. They may alert to strangers or unusual sounds, but are generally manageable with basic training. Consistent "quiet" reinforcement from puppyhood keeps this in check.

faqs.q: Are Caucasian Shepherd Dogs good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs adapt reasonably well to apartment living, particularly if they receive consistent daily walks and indoor enrichment. Their calm nature makes them less disruptive in confined spaces than high-energy large breeds.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Caucasian Shepherd Dog need per day?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs need approximately 30–45 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Caucasian Shepherd Dogs good running partners?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs are lower-energy dogs and are better suited to brisk walks or short jogs than distance running. Long runs can cause joint strain in lower-activity breeds — stick to 20–30 minute jogs rather than endurance runs.

faqs.q: What happens if a Caucasian Shepherd Dog doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Caucasian Shepherd Dog be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Caucasian Shepherd Dog depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A long-line is recommended as an intermediate step for several months.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Caucasian Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: A Caucasian Shepherd Dog needs approximately 3–5 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Caucasian Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Adult Caucasian Shepherd Dogs should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds. For large and giant breeds, twice daily feeding also reduces the risk of bloat (GDV) compared to one large daily meal.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Caucasian Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Lower-energy Caucasian Shepherd Dogs are prone to weight gain — choose a formula with controlled fat content and avoid calorie-dense performance formulas.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Caucasian Shepherd Dog from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Large breeds should stay on a large-breed puppy formula until 18–24 months, then transition to an adult formula. Switching too early can disrupt joint development during the growth phase.

faqs.q: Is a Caucasian Shepherd Dog a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs can be challenging for first-time owners due to their independent temperament. Prior dog experience or professional training classes from the start significantly improves outcomes. Research the breed thoroughly before committing.

faqs.q: Are Caucasian Shepherd Dogs good family dogs?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs can be good family dogs when properly socialised. Their suitability depends more on individual temperament and upbringing than breed alone.

faqs.q: Do Caucasian Shepherd Dogs do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Caucasian Shepherd Dogs form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Caucasian Shepherd Dog?
faqs.a: Plan for 1–1.5 hours per day dedicated to your Caucasian Shepherd Dog — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction. Add 15–30 minutes for grooming 3–4 times weekly. The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
